lookup.scope:
Local recursive-server address lookups across deadline-bounded TCP exchanges.

Checks both query address families and both server socket families. No OS
resolver configuration, cache, retry or query-ID entropy claim.

dns-address-answer.scope:
Pure address-answer selection against an independent record-set model.

Generated DNS packets include binary names, aliases, section separation and
malformed relevant RDATA. This is not a complete stub resolver or DNSSEC test.

dns-tcp-query.scope:
Dedicated DNS TCP query with a deadline spanning setup and response handling.

Local Linux IPv4/IPv6 integration; no resolver policy or upstream suite claim.

limitations: Caller supplies a recursive server and query ID. No OS resolver configuration, entropy allocation, server failover, hosts-file lookup or family ordering.
Each follow-up has its own TCP connection under the same borrowed deadline; this is not a concurrent shared-connection dispatcher.
Empty address results are not cacheable negative-answer proofs. TTL, negative and alias-cache policy remain unimplemented.
Live tests verify query sequences and peer-observed closure, without internal resource-table instrumentation.
